2027-05-22.title: First Saturday of the Apostles
2027-05-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: We are one body in the Spirit
Believe in the one whom he has sent
2027-05-22.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe). Pentecost opened the seven weeks of this season, which recalls the birth of the Church and the mission of the apostles. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and since Pentecost the Angelus (“The Angel of the Lord”) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. Tomorrow, the Second Sunday of the Apostles, the Church keeps the feast of the Most Holy Trinity.
2027-05-22.verse: Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
theo: The first week after Pentecost ends with Paul's great image of the Church: “For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.” Notice the last words. Paul does not say ‘so it is with the Church’, but “so it is with Christ.” The Church is not a club of people who admire Jesus; she is his Body, and he is her Head. At Pentecost the Spirit did not make the apostles a committee; he made them one living organism with the Risen Lord. Paul tells how this happened to each of us: in the one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, and we were all made to drink of one Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:13). Baptism places us in the Body, Chrismation (Confirmation) gives us the Spirit to drink, and the Holy Qurbana, the one Bread, makes us one Body (1 Corinthians 10:17). The Catechism says that the unity of the body does not do away with the diversity of its members (CCC 791).

Then Paul turns playful, and his humour hides a sharp lesson. “If the foot would say, ‘Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,’ that would not make it any less a part of the body.” He imagines an ear sulking because it is not an eye. “If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be?” There are two temptations in a parish. One is envy: I am only a foot, so I am not needed; let the priest and the committee members do everything. The other is pride: I am the eye, and I see everything; the others are useless. Paul answers both with one sentence: “But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.” No one is in the Church by accident. The grandmother who prays the rosary at the back of the church, the altar server who rings the bell, the catechism teacher, the choir singer, the young man who carries chairs after the feast, the sick person offering pain at home: each is placed by God. In the Season of the Apostles, when we recall how the Church was born and sent, we are invited to ask not what the Church does for me, but where God has placed me in the Body.

The Gospel brings us to the morning after the multiplication of the loaves. The crowds have crossed the lake to find Jesus, and he sees through them: “you are looking for me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.” Then he gives one of the great commands of John's Gospel: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.” They ask the practical question: “What must we do to perform the works of God?” And Jesus answers: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.” Faith is not idleness; it is the first and greatest work, the work that God himself does in us and with us. Everything else in the Christian life, our prayer, our service, our place in the Body, flows from believing in the One whom the Father sent. On Saturdays many of our families turn with love to the Blessed Virgin Mary, the first to believe the word of the angel and the Mother whom the apostles gathered around in the upper room (Acts 1:14). She is the model member of the Body: hidden, faithful, and wholly turned towards her Son. With her we learn to seek Jesus not for the bread he gives, but for himself, the Bread that endures for eternal life.
conn: “Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread” (1 Corinthians 10:17).
Paul writes to Rome: “so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually we are members one of another” (Romans 12:5).
Saul, why do you persecute me?
At Damascus the Lord said to Saul, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting” (Acts 9:5): to strike the Body is to strike the Head.
“He is the head of the body, the church” (Colossians 1:18).
Isaiah asks, “Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread?” (Isaiah 55:2).
After the Ascension the apostles devoted themselves to prayer “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the many members receive the one Body and become what they receive: the Body of Christ gathered around the one altar.
Jesus gives the food that endures for eternal life: the Bread we receive at the Qurbana is the Son of Man himself, on whom the Father has set his seal.
outline: A body in which the foot complains and the ear sulks.
Point 1 · So it is with Christ
The Church, his Body, born of the Spirit.
Point 2 · As God arranged, as he chose
No one in the Body by accident.
Point 3 · This is the work of God: believe
The food that endures, and the faith of Mary.
A parish feast in Kuttanad where the youngest boy proudly folds the chairs while the elders sing the Lord's praises.
“This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
live: Ask your parish priest or a council member where help is needed, and offer one hour this month.
Thank one person in your parish whose service no one notices.
Work for the bread that endures (John 6:27)
Before your next meal, pray: Lord, give me also the bread that endures for eternal life.
On this Saturday pray a decade of the rosary for the unity of the Church.
fathers: If you are the body of Christ and his members, it is your own mystery that is placed on the Lord's table; it is your own mystery that you receive. Be what you see, and receive what you are.
Why do you prepare your teeth and your stomach? Believe, and you have eaten. To believe in him whom the Father sent is to eat the living Bread.
magis: Believers who respond to God's word become members of Christ's Body; the unity of the body does not do away with the diversity of its members.
The unity of the Mystical Body: the Eucharist makes the Church.
Believing in Jesus Christ and in the One who sent him is necessary for salvation; faith is a gift of God that we must nourish and persevere in.
After her Son's Ascension, Mary aided the beginnings of the Church by her prayers; she was present in the upper room praying for the gift of the Spirit.
saints: First Saturday of the Apostles. In the Latin calendar, St Rita of Cascia, religious. The First Set lists St Rita on 23 May, where she gives way to the Trinity this year.

16–22 May: first week of the Season of the Apostles. Mon 17: Mary, Mother of the Church. Thu 20: anniversary of the inauguration of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993); in the Latin calendar, St Bernardine of Siena. Fri 21: the Friday of Gold; in the Latin calendar, St Christopher Magallanes and companions. Sat 22: in the Latin calendar, St Rita of Cascia. Sun 23: Second Sunday of the Apostles, the feast of the Most Holy Trinity; St Rita, listed for 23 May in the First Set, gives way to the feast (verify locally).
2027-05-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Head of the Church, by the one Spirit you baptized us into one Body and gave us one Spirit to drink. Forgive us when we envy the gifts of others or despise our own place; help each of us to serve where the Father has placed us. Give us hunger for the food that endures for eternal life, and the faith that is the work of God. With the Blessed Virgin Mary, who prayed with the apostles in the upper room, may we seek you for yourself and remain one in you, to the glory of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Amen.

quick: Paul: the body is one and has many members; so it is with Christ.
Paul: God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.
Jesus: work for the food that endures for eternal life; this is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.
2027-05-22.action: Offer one hour of hidden service to your parish this month.
2027-05-22.question: Do I seek Jesus for himself, or only for what he gives me?
kidsaint: Rita lived in Italy long ago. She was a wife and mother whose husband was hot-tempered; she prayed for him with great patience until he changed. After he died she became a nun. People call her the saint of impossible things, because she trusted God when everything seemed hopeless. The Latin Church remembers her on 22 May.
2027-05-22.special: First Saturday of the Apostles. Eve of the feast of the Most Holy Trinity.
term: Paul's name for the Church: the faithful, joined by Baptism and the Eucharist to Christ their Head and to one another as members, each with a different gift from the one Spirit. The same words name the Holy Eucharist, the sacrament that makes the Church one Body.

family.explain: Our body has many parts: eyes to see, ears to hear, hands to work and feet to walk. Imagine if the foot said, ‘I am not a hand, so I am not part of the body!’ That would be silly. Paul says the Church is like a body, and Jesus is the head. In our family and our parish everyone has a different job, and all are needed.
family.intention: We pray for everyone in our parish, especially those whose work no one sees.
family.ask: Ask: “What is my job in our family and in our parish? How can I do it with love?”

illus: At a parish feast in Kuttanad, a small boy of seven was upset because his older brother was carrying the processional cross and he was only allowed to fold chairs. His grandmother took him aside. ‘Monae, if no one folds the chairs, where will the people sit for the next feast? The cross goes ahead, the chairs come after, and the Lord sees both.’ That evening the boy folded more chairs than anyone, and the parish priest thanked him by name at the end of the Qurbana. Years later, as a young man, he still remembered it as the day he learned that the Church is a body.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Head of the Body, we are many, but we are one in you. Fill us with the Spirit we drank in Baptism, and make us one heart as we pray. Amen.
share: For just as the body is one and has many members… so it is with Christ (1 Corinthians 12:12). Do I see myself as a living member of Christ's Body?
God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose (1 Corinthians 12:18). Where has God placed me to serve?
You are looking for me… because you ate your fill of the loaves (John 6:26). Why do I seek Jesus?
This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent (John 6:29). How can I strengthen my faith this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one Body in you.
interc: For the unity of the Church, that all members may honour one another's gifts.
For those who feel useless or unwanted in the Church, that they may find their place in the Body.
For the hungry of the world, that they may receive bread, and for all of us, that we may hunger for the bread of eternal life.
For our parishes, that they may welcome every member, the strong and the weak.
Through the prayers of the Blessed Virgin Mary, for a deeper faith in our families.
pm.close: Father, by the one Spirit you made us one Body in your Son. Keep us united in faith and love, and feed us with the bread that endures for eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on this Saturday after Pentecost, Paul describes the Church as a body. “For just as the body is one and has many members… so it is with Christ.”
The Church is the Body of Christ, and he is the Head. In Baptism we were placed in that Body, and we drank the one Spirit.

Paul jokes about a foot that says, I am not a hand, so I do not belong. And an ear that says, I am not an eye. How foolish! Every part is needed. “God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.”
In our parish there is no unimportant member: the one who sings, the one who teaches, the one who cleans, the one who prays in a sickbed at home. Each is placed by God.
In the Gospel the people follow Jesus because he gave them bread. Jesus says: work for the food that endures for eternal life. And the work of God is this: to believe in the One whom he has sent.
Like the Blessed Virgin Mary, who prayed with the apostles, let us seek Jesus for himself, and serve him gladly in the place he has given us. Amen.
kids: Children, can your eye say to your hand, ‘I don't need you’? No! Your body needs every part. The Church is like that: everyone is important, even the smallest child.
What is your part? Maybe singing, maybe helping, maybe praying for others. Do it with joy, because you belong to Jesus' Body!

intro: Theme: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
The Church, the one Body of Christ with many members, each placed by God, and faith as the first work, learnt with the Blessed Virgin Mary.

sub: Baptized into one Body, made to drink of one Spirit.
The Church, the Body of the Risen Lord.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.
points.apply: Pray this week for someone in your parish with whom you find unity difficult.

points.h: As God arranged, as he chose
sub: The foot that envies the hand.
The eye that despises the ear.
No one in the Body by accident.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.
points.apply: Offer one hour of service to your parish this month, in the place where help is needed.

sub: Working for the food of eternal life.
Faith, the work of God, with Mary.
q: Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For it is on him that God the Father has set his seal.
points.apply: Before each meal this week, ask for the bread that endures for eternal life, and receive the Qurbana with renewed faith.

concl: We are one Body in Christ, each member placed by God and needed by all.
Let us seek Jesus for himself, and believe in the One whom the Father has sent.
2027-05-22.resolve: This week, find your place of service in the parish, thank one hidden member, and pray a decade of the rosary for the unity of the Church.
